# **Horse Prediction Market (Polymarekit)**

**Student Name:** Rylee Hilde  
**Course:** CS 408 \- Full Stack Web Development  
**Semester:** Fall 2026

---

## **Overview**

The project I intend to build is called Polymarekit, a full-stack web application designed to model a **prediction market for horses**. This application will of course be based on fake trends and conversion rates themed around horses if they could gamble. The general theme of the application is a **betting market for horses**, with a focus on providing a prediction market with fake currency conversion rates, dynamic trends to predict on, fake news to influence trends,  etc. 

The core problem this application solves is the lack of accessibility for horses to gamble in a prediction market. I think horses should have the ability to participate in a prediction market and be able to diversify their financial portfolio. Polymarekit will have a web interface that will list out the different options to predict on as well as price conversions for each.

Polymarekit takes conceptual inspiration from real prediction markets like polymarket. Unlike these platforms it will represent fake data and currency to predict on. This program will focus on providing a realistic experience using fake data.

The backend of the application will run on **AWS EC2**, using **Django and Gunicorn/Nginx**, with data stored in a **SQLite database**. The frontend will use **Django Templates** rendered server-side and styled with **Tailwind CSS**.

This project meets all minimum requirements by including:

* Multiple pages for the different markets, overview page, profile, wallet funds, price conversion, etc. with shared navigation  
* Forms that submit data to AWS for different markets names, or wallet configuration  
* Database retrieval, conditional retrieval, and deletion   
* Deployment scripts for EC2  
* Styling applied across all pages


## **Target Audience**

The primary target audience for Polymarekit is for **horses**, particularly horses interested in investments in the prediction market. These users encounter opportunities with their finances to invest and hopefully profit from their investments.

Secondary audiences include:

* Non-horses (which can include humans and several other animals)

The application is useful because it provides:

* Clear view of the markets that you are interested in  
* Price conversions as the rates change over time  
* View of your funds and options to change or add more to your funds

The niche served by Polymarekit is horses who want an accessible, effortless investment opportunities in the prediction market, rather than using the prediction market apps used today that are designed for humans.

## **Functionality**

### **Home Page**

* Acts as the homepage of the application  
* Lists all available prediction markets to invest in  
* Explains what the app does and who it is for (this will only trigger when the account is first registered as an onboarding process)  
* Includes navigation links to all other pages

### **Profile Page**

* Shows Profile attributes for user  
* Shows:  
  * Username  
  * Profile status  
  * Description  
  * Profile picture  
* Includes buttons to:  
  * Edit profile attribute  
* Submits update to database that manages profile attributes  
* Submits data to the backend running on AWS EC2  
* Stores submitted data in the SQLite database

### **Wallet Page**

* Shows total funds in account and breakdowns of currency  
* Submits update to database whenever “funds” are added  
* **NOTE:** Funds are absolutely going to be fake. The “currency” is going to be fake as well. The types of “funds” that will be accepted are carrots, apples, horseshoes, and hay. The user can add as much currency as they want in this implementation  
* Submits/Requests data to the backend running on AWS EC2  
* Stores/Requests submitted data in the SQLite database

### **Market Page**

* Displays details for a **single market**  
* The home page will list all of the markets  
* The markets will be dynamically generated (up to 5-10) and stored in the database once they get generated so you can see the market whenever. Markets will update trending upward or downwards depending on trend generated  
* Users on this page can buy or sell stock using their wallet funds  
* When an investment happens, the user’s wallet and investment records will update with the value and currency that they invest  
* Submits data to the backend running on AWS EC2  
* Stores submitted data in the SQLite database

### **Portfolio Page**

* Shows each user’s current investments grouped by market and currency  
* Calculates the current value of the user’s holdings from stored investments and market values  
* Requests data to the backend running on AWS EC2  
* Requests data in the SQLite database

### **Trade History Page**

* Shows the user’s previous buy and sell transactions  
* Displays the market, amount, currency, transaction type, and date for each trade  
* Requests data to the backend running on AWS EC2  
* Requests data in the SQLite database

### **Market Search and Filter Page**

* Searches markets by name  
* Filters markets by current value or upward/downward trend  
* Links to the selected market’s detail page  
* Requests data to the backend running on AWS EC2  
* Requests data in the SQLite database

### **About Us Pages**

* About Us shows the company description, mission, and purpose for horses interested in the prediction market

All pages will share a **common header and footer**, implemented using Django Templates.

**Database Schema**

The application will use a SQLite database containing four primary tables named profile\_wallet, markets, investments.

### **Table: profile\_wallet**

| Column Name | Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| id | INTEGER | Primary key, auto-increment |
| username | TEXT | Profile username |
| description | TEXT | Profile description |
| status | TEXT | Profile status |
| wallet\_total | INTEGER | Total amount of “funds” (carrots, apples, horseshoes, hay) |
| carrots | INTEGER | Total carrots (contribute toward wallet total) |
| apples | INTEGER | Total apples (contribute toward wallet total) |
| horseshoes | INTEGER | Total horseshoes (contribute toward wallet total) |
| hay | INTEGER | Total hay (contribute toward wallet total) |

This schema supports:

* Creating an account  
* Updating funds  
* Retrieving fund breakdown   
* Update profile attributes  
* Deleting an account

### **Table: markets**

| Column Name | Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| id | INTEGER | Primary key, auto-increment |
| market\_name | TEXT | Name of market |
| market\_value | INTEGER | Starting value of market (increases or decreases based on trend) |

This schema supports:

* Requesting markets from predetermined bank of markets  
* Giving starting value to start trends

### **Table: investments**

| Column Name | Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| id | INTEGER | Primary key, auto-increment |
| profile\_id  | INTEGER | Foreign key referencing the user profile |
| market\_id | INTEGER | Foreign key referencing the market |
| amount  | INTEGER | Amount bought or sold |
| currency | TEXT | Currency |
| transaction\_type | TEXT | Buy or sell |
| created\_at  | DATETIME | Date and time of the transactions |

This schema supports:

* Investing in a market

The schema may be adjusted slightly during development, but this structure satisfies the project requirements.

## **Tech Stack**

This project will use the **Django/Python stack**:

* **Backend Language:** Python  
* **Backend Framework:** Django  
* **Database:** SQLite  
* **Frontend Templates:** Django Templates  
* **Frontend Styling:** Tailwind CSS  
* **Hosting Platform:** AWS EC2 (Ubuntu)

## **EC2 Setup and Configuration**

### **EC2 Setup Script**

A bash script will:

* Update system packages  
* Install python3  
* Install SQLite  
* Install project dependencies with requirements.txt and pip

### **App Configuration Script**

A second script will:

* Set environment variables  
* Initialize the database  
* Start the Django server

### **Running the Application**

1. Launch an EC2 instance  
2. SSH into the instance  
3. Run the setup script  
4. Run the configuration script  
5. Access the app via the public IP and port

Detailed instructions will be provided in the project README.

## **Project Schedule (7 Checkpoints)**

### **Checkpoint 1 \- Configure EC2 and run the Django application**

* ### Complete the EC2 setup and app configuration scripts

* ### Install dependencies, initialize SQLite, and verify the deployed app is reachable

### **Checkpoint 2 \- Build the Django foundation, shared navigation, and Home Page**

* ### Set up the Django project, templates, Tailwind styling, and shared header/footer

* ### Display available markets on the Home Page

### **Checkpoint 3 \- Implement accounts, Profile Page, and Wallet Page**

* ### Add account creation and deletion

* ### Add profile editing and wallet fund updates

* ### Populate and retrieve the profile\_wallet data

### **Checkpoint 4 \- Implement markets and the Market Page**

* ### Populate markets with starting values and generated trends

* ### Add market detail views and buy/sell forms

### **Checkpoint 5 \- Add investment storage, Portfolio Page, and Trade History Page**

* ### Store each buy and sell transaction in the investments table

* ### Display current holdings and the user’s complete trade history

### **Checkpoint 6 \- Add Market Search and Filter Page and complete navigation**

* ### Search markets by name

* ### Filter markets by value and trend

* ### Link Home, Search, Market, Portfolio, Trade History, Wallet, and Profile pages

### **Checkpoint 7 \- Finish static information pages and horse-themed styling**

* ### Add the static About Us page

* ### Apply the final horse-themed styling and verify all pages work together

## **Summary of Changes**

The changes to this document were adding a couple more pages with dynamic content like the trade history page, portfolio page, and market history page. I also added a database table schema specifically for investments to track what investments have been made and when it was bought or sold. This will be great to connect the databases together with foreign keys and such so I am excited to implement those database relations in this project. The checkpoints have also been reworked so that EC2 configuration and scripting is first to be completed and also added more descriptive and assessable requirements for each checkpoint. There were also some pages added so I added the descriptions for that and added them under the checkpoints to be completed. As for the peer reviews, I did not include detailed testing as the testing will be ad-hoc testing where the functioning of the website will serve as tests passing. I have also reduced my page count due to my peer reviews. I have taken out my news and careers pages and left my about us page as they are all going to be static pages and I only really wanted one of them to add to my page count. Plus, the careers and news pages very minimally contribute to the goal of the project.
